public_rationale: On the day of the demo, TechCrunch reported that o3 was not widely available. Only safety researchers could sign up, for an o3-mini preview, with an o3 preview to follow later. OpenAI released o3 on 16 April 2025. The benchmark claims at the reveal came from OpenAI's internal evaluations. ARC Prize did test o3, but he named that exception himself. So both parts hold.
limitations: 'Vetted by the scientific community' has no precise test. ARC Prize's evaluation is a partial independent check, which he acknowledged.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of the demo, o3 had not been released to the public nor vetted by the scientific community.

statement.excerpt: The product was not yet released to the general public; it’s not been vetted by the scientific community.
statement.document_title: o3, AGI, the art of the demo, and what you can expect in 2025

from_speaker: The product was not yet released to the general public

our_interpretation: Plain reading: on 20–21 December 2024, o3 was not available to the public, and outside researchers had not broadly evaluated it. The ARC Prize test is an exception he states himself, so it does not count against him.
Applications for early safety-testing access do not count as public release or scientific vetting.
criteria.support_condition: Records show o3 was not publicly available on 20–21 December 2024, was released later, and its benchmark results at that time were mainly OpenAI's own.
criteria.contradiction_condition: o3 was publicly available by 21 December 2024, or independent researchers beyond ARC Prize had broadly evaluated it by then.
